questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was nice that it was in europe, and that the university offered some very nice courses fitting to my specific interest of my field of study.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My university abroad was very structured and easy to adapt to, and the courses was very interesting. A little downside was that the uni required much more readings that i am used to.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I though it was a bit hard to navigate in all the mails with information from my home uni, the uni abroad and Erasmus. I though i got so many mails (some more relevant than others) and it was hard to know when the information was crusial or just good to know. And also a bit hard to remember, when wanting to look up the information, who the information was provied by.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The abroad uni was very good to send out news letters, where they had an event at uni called introduction to uni, that was very helpfull.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got it through the uni, so it was easy and without any problems.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it can be quiet far away from uni, from what we are used to in kbh.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I overall though it was great, but i had a problem that the studen thousing (i got through uni) ended before my semester at the uni ended, so i had 4 days in the end of my stay without any housing, that was a big problem for me, and i think many had the same problem.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They had a zoom meeting explaining how to do it which was very helpful.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I could apply for 56 etcs point and then they made lottery and assigned me to courses of 30 etcs. I only got 24 etcs in first round and then i had to apply again in second round.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They had a zoom meeting explaining how to do it which was very helpful. And it was possible to send mails and get quick replies!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the first round i only got 24 etcs of wanted courses, so for second round i had to apply again for a course of 6, and then i had to pick a course of the ones with free spots, and it was courses which did not really fit my field of study, so that was a bit unfortunate.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be in contact with the exchange office at the abroad uni, they are very helpful, and can help make exceptions also.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level similar to the ones at KU, but they all required much more readings of scientific articles that i am used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I only had lectures, where as at KU im used to a mix of lectures and tutourials and classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Topic; Organisations in the media
Education and work
Topic; Political communication, campaigns and voters
Topic; Always connected, youth, media and technology
Topic; The language of strategic communication

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would really recommend all of the topic courses: The language of strategic communication, Always connected, youth, media and technology, Organisations in the media, Political communication, campaigns and voters.

They were all very relevant for the wants of working as a communication professional in the future. They used very recent examples and the lecturers were very competent and empathic and kind. They all had much readings but it was all mostly recent studies which made it very interesting readings.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Expensive to use public transportation (more than in dk)
Supermarked was probably the same, but maybe a bit less than dk, and then some specific things were more expensive 
Less expensive to go out for drinks and food (less than in dk)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had a whole day in the intro week telling about the all sports and opportunities at uni.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined my local yoga studio, it was nice to have a routine when moving to another city.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend going to the citys in the netherlands not far from Amsterdam; Utrecht, Rotterdam, Haag and Gent (in belgium).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the culture in Amsterdam seems very similar to the danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I did not really get any dutch friends at all. But it was super easy to get in contact with other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
It is not a difference, but dutch people are a bit closed like danish people, and the studens spoke dutch to each other even though it was english lectures. This made it hard to get any dutch friends at lectures. 

But in generel Amsterdam is a very english speaking country, and it was super easy to get in contact with new people and getting new friends.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Making new friends, and experiencing how it is to create a new everyday in a new city.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go to the introweek, it was there i made contact to the persons who became my friends at the stay.
Rent a bike so you can get around.
Use the provided study halls at uni they are very nice.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
That the exchange office and service helpdisk at uni are very helpful and quick to reply.

And also that the lecturers are very kind and helpful too.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
The academic gain from my courses have been crucial to the direction i want to go further in my studies and carreer.
Getting new friends. 
Being forced to practice my english, being more comfortable speaking english even though i still do gramma mistakes and have a danish accent.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting new friends while speaking english.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
